issues.description: HTTP method mapping for the "create person" endpoint is inconsistent between the problem statement, the client, and the solution. The problem statement and client expect POST /persons (Problem: lines 109-114; Client: PersonController.addPerson uses webClient.post().uri("persons") ), but the solution's server registers the creation endpoint with @PutMapping("persons") instead of @PostMapping("persons"). This mismatch will cause the client POST requests to /persons to get 404/405 responses or not hit the intended handler, confusing students and preventing the client-server interaction from working as described.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the server-side mapping for creating a Person to use POST. Replace @PutMapping("persons") with @PostMapping("persons") (and keep the method name createPerson). Ensure the server import for PostMapping is present. This aligns the server with the problem statement and the client (which sends a POST to /persons).

issues.description: The problem statement specifies the create-person endpoint as POST /persons (and the client controller expects to call POST /persons), but the solution implementation maps the createPerson method with @PutMapping("persons"). This mismatches the HTTP method used to represent the same conceptual action (creating a new Person). Students implementing the server from the problem description or following the client will expect a POST endpoint; the solution's use of PUT for creation is an unintended semantic mismatch that will break the mapping between requirement, client code, and server implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the server create endpoint with the problem statement and client by using POST. Change the annotation on the server's createPerson method to @PostMapping("persons") (instead of @PutMapping), so the endpoint is POST /persons and matches the client webClient.post(...) call and the problem description.
